definitions.explanation: The number 8,000. {八|はち} shortens to {はっ} before {千|せん}, so the reading is はっせん, never はちせん.

examples.english: That will be eight thousand yen.

examples.japanese: この{山|やま}は{八千|はっせん}メートル{級|きゅう}ではない。
examples.english: This mountain is not in the eight-thousand-meter class.

examples.japanese: {昨年度|さくねんど}の{来場者|らいじょうしゃ}は{八千|はっせん}{人|にん}を{超|こ}え、{過去|かこ}{最多|さいた}となった。
examples.english: Last year's attendance exceeded eight thousand, the highest on record.

notes:
One of the three irregular thousands. The {はち} → {はっ} shortening also appears in {八百|はっぴゃく} (800) and {八本|はっぽん} (eight long objects).

SOUND CHANGES IN THE THOUSANDS:
- {一千|いっせん}: 1,000
- {三千|さんぜん}: 3,000
- {八千|はっせん}: 8,000
- all others are regular: {四千|よんせん}, {五千|ごせん}, {六千|ろくせん}, {七千|ななせん}, {九千|きゅうせん}

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {八千|はっせん}{円|えん}: eight thousand yen
- {八千|はっせん}{人|にん}: eight thousand people
- {八千|はっせん}メートル{級|きゅう}: of the eight-thousand-meter class, said of the world's highest peaks
